ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Imagine that snakes were no longer present in this ecosystem. What is a likely effect on the mouse population?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a food web diagram, with arrows indicating food or prey pointing to predators. In the diagram, Grass can be seen pointing to Mouse, indicating that mice feed on grass; at the same time, there is an arrow connection between Mouse and Snake, with the direction pointing to Snake, indicating that snakes prey on mice. Reasoning: If there are no longer snakes in this ecosystem, the pressure on mice from snake predation will decrease. Because grass can still provide food for mice, after snakes disappear, mice are more likely to survive and reproduce. Therefore, the mouse population may increase.
